Tuesday, November 17

Game recap

MTL1NYR3Final: MTL 1, NYR 3

The Rangers threw themselves a centennial party at the Garden and Will Cuylle showed up as both the DJ and the bouncer. Montreal actually scored first, Phillip Danault finishing a Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson setup midway through the second, and that lead lasted a whole 1:48 before Cuylle tied it. Then, with 57 seconds left in the period and the Canadiens on a power play, Cuylle scored again, shorthanded, off an Adam Fox feed, which is the hockey version of getting robbed in your own driveway. Scott Morrow added his first of the season in the third, and Joonas Korpisalo did the rest with 24 saves on 25 shots. Jacob Fowler stopped 23 of 26 and deserved a better night. That's three straight wins for New York and two straight losses for Montreal, whose power play just turned a Rangers birthday party into a gift exchange.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN3UTA2Final: VAN 3, UTA 2

Lock the doors, the Canucks have a winning streak. Two whole games. Nikita Tolopilo made his season debut and treated Utah's 36 shots like spam calls, stopping 34 of them, while Vancouver needed only 24 shots of its own to steal a 3-2 win in Salt Lake City. Brock Boeser ran the show with a goal and two assists: he set up Jake DeBrusk's power-play opener, fed Filip Chytil for a 2-1 lead, then buried the winner himself on another power play with 4:23 left. Utah tied it twice in the third, on Vincent Trocheck's power-play goal and Barrett Hayton's equalizer, and Logan Cooley picked up an assist in his return. None of it mattered. Karel Vejmelka gave up three on 24, and the Mammoth are now six games without a win, the last of them to the team in the league's basement. Extinction usually takes longer than this.

Monday, November 16

Game recap

EDM5PHI2Final: EDM 5, PHI 2

The Oilers went to Philadelphia and treated it like a layover. Edmonton won 5-2, scored twice on the power play in the first and led 3-0 after one, with Leon Draisaitl scoring on the first power play and Vasily Podkolzin, unassisted, on the second. Zach Hyman made it 3-0 for his 500th career point. Cole Knuble and Noah Cates got Philly back within 3-2 in the second, and for one intermission it looked like a game. Then Draisaitl scored 1:07 into the third for his 20th goal, and Connor McDavid put the empty-netter away to finish with a goal and two assists and stretch his point streak to 22 games. Tristan Jarry stopped 34 of 36; Dan Vladar stopped 16 of 19. Edmonton is 9-0-1 on the road. The Flyers are still scoring 2.30 goals a game, the fewest in the league, an offense that's been saving its goals like they're for a rainy day.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA1DAL2OTFinal: FLA 1, DAL 2 OT

Florida and Dallas combined for three goals in 63 minutes, and the Stars got the last one. Matthew Tkachuk opened the scoring on a second-period power play for his 700th career point, then Wyatt Johnston tied it under five minutes later. That was it until overtime, when Jason Robertson finished a Roope Hintz feed at 2:56 for his 10th of the year and a 2-1 Stars win. Casey DeSmith stopped 25 of 26 and Akira Schmid 20 of 22. Thomas Harley played 30:54 with Miro Heiskanen out a fifth straight game, which is less a shift pattern than a hostage situation. Brady Tkachuk threw 10 hits and Colin Blackwell matched him, so plenty of people got hit and almost nobody scored. Florida took a point on the second night of a back-to-back and is 2-0-1 this week, but a power play goal and nothing after it is the kind of night that has the Panthers counting the days until Barkov's back.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1ANA6Final: CGY 1, ANA 6

Calgary won in Los Angeles on Saturday and then spent Sunday paying for it in Anaheim, 6-1. Jeff Malott scored 1:16 in, and Cutter Gauthier made it 2-0 later in the first, which means he has now scored in nine straight games, the NHL's longest streak in 29 years and two short of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record. Beckett Sennecke had two goals and an assist, one of them into an empty net, Mikael Granlund added a goal and an assist, and Tim Washe scored too. Mikael Backlund's goal early in the third made it 3-1 for all of 25 seconds before Sennecke answered. Ian Moore got an assist in his season debut. Ville Husso stopped 20 of 21, and Devin Cooley, on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped 28 of 33. The Flames are -23 on the season, a goal differential that reads less like a stat and more like a cry for help.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6VGK3Final: VAN 6, VGK 3

The last-place Canucks walked into T-Mobile Arena and won 6-3, which is the kind of upset Vegas usually charges admission for. Elias Pettersson scored on a first-period power play and Linus Karlsson and Filip Chytil made it 3-1 by the first intermission. Chytil's first two goals of the season came back to back, the second one shorthanded. Mark Stone's power-play goal early in the third pulled Vegas within 4-3 and tied the Golden Knights' franchise points record at 417, and 24 seconds later Drew O'Connor restored the two-goal lead. Karlsson's empty-netter capped his two-goal night, and Brock Boeser had two assists. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 34 of 37. Carter Hart stopped 21 of 26. Vancouver is still 4-17-1, but Vegas just lost at home to the team everyone else in the league is using as a tune-up, which should be a fun film session.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH2SJS4Final: NSH 2, SJS 4

Nashville's seven-game win streak ended in San Jose, against a Sharks team that had played in Utah the night before. Will Smith and Collin Graf scored in the first, Ivar Stenberg made it 3-0 early in the second, and Macklin Celebrini put it away in the third, with Celebrini and Smith each finishing with a goal and two assists. Nils Hoglander and a late Steven Stamkos power-play goal were all the Predators had to show. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 32 of 34; Juuse Saros stopped 20 of 24. The Sharks have won two in a row and three of their last four, with the kids doing the heavy lifting. Nashville flew all the way to California to remember what losing feels like, courtesy of a Sharks team that's still -18 on the season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, November 15

Game recap

SEA1CAR5Final: SEA 1, CAR 5

Carolina packed up Helsinki with a 5-1 win and a two-game sweep of Seattle, which is a long way to fly to get your homework graded twice. The power play did the damage: Jackson Blake opened it up with the man advantage, and Andrei Svechnikov scored twice more on it, with Nikolaj Ehlers setting up three goals. Mark Jankowski chipped in two of his own, and Jordan Staal played 13:55 in his first game back after missing 14. Joey Daccord was pulled after letting in four on 14 shots, Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 23 the rest of the way, and Matty Beniers got Seattle's only goal. Pyotr Kochetkov needed just 12 saves, and Jagger Firkus made his NHL debut in a game that was over by the second intermission. The Kraken put 13 shots on net across a whole hockey game, about what they'd manage from the Climate Pledge parking lot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG5CHI4SOFinal: WPG 5, CHI 4 SO

Chicago led 4-0 midway through the second period and still lost, which takes a special kind of commitment. Tyler Bertuzzi, Anton Frondell and Connor Bedard (power play) chased Stuart Skinner after one period (three goals on eight shots), Frank Nazar made it 4-0 on another power play, and then the Blackhawks went back to being the Blackhawks. Mark Scheifele started the comeback at 16:05 of the second, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti (power play) followed, and Gabriel Vilardi tied it with 1:13 left and the goalie pulled. Scheifele finished with a goal and three assists, set the Jets' franchise points record, and scored in the shootout too; Connor added the winner there, with Patrick Kane the only Hawk to beat Nico Daws, who stopped 12 of 13 in relief. Spencer Knight made 27 saves. In Chicago a four-goal lead isn't a cushion, it's a loan, and the Jets called it in.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN6BOS2Final: MIN 6, BOS 2

Minnesota walked into TD Garden and treated it like a rental: 6-2, an eighth straight road win and an 11-game point streak. Ryan Hartman scored twice, Danila Yurov scored twice (the second into an empty net), and Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman also scored, Coleman adding two assists. Kirill Kaprizov set up two, and Brock Faber got an assist in his season debut, the kind of welcome-back gift most guys only get in their dreams. Fraser Minten on the power play and David Pastrnak cut it to 4-2, then Yurov answered 90 seconds later. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 of 32; Jeremy Swayman saw 24 shots and let five through. Marcus Foligno and Tanner Jeannot fought in the second, which was Boston's best stretch of the night. The Bruins wanted a statement game and got one: it just had the Wild's name on it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM1TOR0Final: EDM 1, TOR 0

Devon Levi got his first NHL shutout, and Toronto made it easy for him: 19 shots, all saved, in a 1-0 Oilers win. The only goal came at 15:34 of the second, Evan Bouchard finishing off Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, which stretches McDavid's point streak to 21 games. Anthony Stolarz was terrific at the other end, 22 saves on 23, and got exactly the run support he's come to expect. John Tavares thought he'd tied it late, but the goal was waved off, the perfect ending to a homestand the Leafs finished 0-6, now six straight losses. Colton Dach and Brandon Duhaime fought in the first, the closest Toronto came to winning anything all night. Leafs fans paid full price to watch a team that can't score in its own building, which at least makes it a very Toronto tradition.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL4MTL1Final: COL 4, MTL 1

Colorado played its first game without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar and won 4-1 in Montreal anyway, which is either great depth or a very bad sign for the Canadiens. It ended Montreal's 12-game point streak. Fedor Svechkov opened the scoring, Brock Nelson made it 2-0 with an extra attacker on late in the first, and after Nick Suzuki got one back in the second, Artturi Lehkonen scored his 15th on the power play and Nicolas Roy hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 26, Jakub Dobes 23 of 26. Alex Gagne made his NHL debut beside Brent Burns, who played his 1,600th game, so the Avs' blue line went from first night to forever on one pair. Montreal spent two weeks looking like a contender and then lost to the Avalanche's understudies.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET2TBL0Final: DET 2, TBL 0

Daniil Tarasov stopped all 31 shots and Detroit won 2-0 in Tampa, ending its five-game skid and the Lightning's home streak in one go. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal that mattered, at 13:12 of the second from William Wallinder, and set up Michael Brandsegg-Nygård's empty-netter with 43 seconds left. Andrei Vasilevskiy was nearly as good, 20 saves on 21, and lost anyway, because Tampa played without Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak and couldn't solve a goalie who got the start after John Gibson gave up five in Florida. The Red Wings needed a win like they need Dylan Larkin to pick up the phone, and they got one. Tampa had 31 shots and zero goals, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT4PIT1Final: OTT 4, PIT 1

Linus Ullmark picked up his 200th NHL win in Pittsburgh, and the Penguins barely made him work for it: 16 saves on 17 in a 4-1 Senators win that runs Ottawa's point streak to five. Tommy Novak gave Pittsburgh a lead with eight seconds left in the first, and that was the last fun the home crowd had. Michael Amadio tied it with an unassisted goal and then set up Claude Giroux, Tim Stützle added his 11th in the third, and Thomas Chabot finished it into the empty net. Sergei Murashov kept it close with 30 saves on 33. Ottawa outshot Pittsburgh 34-17, which is the kind of gap you usually see between the NHL and the AHL. The Penguins are 7-11-2 and Kyle Dubas is reportedly warming up the sell button, and nights like this are why.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD7WSH4Final: NJD 7, WSH 4

Washington threw 47 shots at Connor Hellebuyck, scored four, and still lost 7-4, because the Devils got their own goalie and the Capitals got whatever Charlie Lindgren was doing (26 saves on 32). Hellebuyck made 43 saves and is 7-0-0 as a Devil, a franchise record. The Caps led three times in the first, 1-0, 2-1 and 3-2, on goals from Pierre-Luc Dubois, Ryan Leonard and Anthony Beauvillier, and Cole Hutson set up three. Then New Jersey took over: Jesper Boqvist tied it, Timo Meier scored on the power play, and Nico Hischier's shorthanded goal 56 seconds into the third was the winner. Evan Rodrigues scored twice, Lenni Hameenaho had a goal and two assists, and Luke Hughes three assists, while Anton Silaev made his NHL debut. The Capitals outshot the Devils by 15 and lost by three, which is advanced stats' way of saying 'nice try.'

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI4CBJ3Final: PHI 4, CBJ 3

Columbus scored twice in the first 4:19 on home ice, and the Flyers, a team that scores like it's paying per goal, answered with four. Dmitri Voronkov's first of the season and Matthew Knies put the Blue Jackets up 2-0. Trevor Zegras, an unassisted Matvei Michkov and a Denver Barkey power-play goal made it 3-2 early in the second; Adam Fantilli tied it, and Barkey won it at 11:54 of the third off Noel Acciari's setup. Joseph Woll stopped 28 of 31, Jet Greaves 17 of 21, and Owen Tippett and Dante Fabbro fought in the second. Columbus played without Sean Monahan and is 7-11-0. Blowing a two-goal lead to the Flyers' offense is like getting outrun by a Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA4STL1Final: FLA 4, STL 1

St. Louis honored Keith Tkachuk before the game, and his sons said thanks by beating the Blues: Brady Tkachuk scored the power-play opener, with Matthew Tkachuk on the assist, in a 4-1 Florida win. Dmitry Kulikov scored his first of the season a minute later, Anton Lundell made it 3-0 in the second, and Sam Reinhart's unassisted goal in the third, his 12th, came on a night he reached 700 career points. Jacob Markstrom stopped 23 of 24 and lost the shutout to Dylan Holloway's power-play goal with 2:06 left. Joel Hofer made 24 saves on 28 in his fourth straight start. Radko Gudas played his 900th game. It was a lovely ceremony for the Tkachuk family, and then the family took two points home to Florida, the most Blues thing imaginable.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF0DAL2Final: BUF 0, DAL 2

Jamie Benn got his 1,000th career point, every one of them in a Dallas sweater, and it was the goal that beat Buffalo 2-0. Benn scored at 16:23 of the second off Justin Hryckowian and Nils Lundkvist, and Wyatt Johnston added a power-play goal with 42 seconds left. Jake Oettinger needed only 22 saves for his fourth shutout, which says a lot about the Sabres' night. Alex Lyon was good in his second straight start, 28 saves on 30, and got nothing for it. Dallas is 11-6-2; Buffalo is 8-8-4 and has now been shut out by a goalie who could have played the third period in a recliner. A thousand points for Benn, zero for the Sabres: that's been the Buffalo experience for about 15 years.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS6UTA5SOFinal: SJS 6, UTA 5 SO

Ten goals in 65 minutes, two fights and a shootout, and San Jose came out of Utah with a 6-5 win and Utah with a fifth straight loss. Zac Jones scored twice as Utah led 3-1 and 4-3, but the Sharks kept coming: Tyler Toffoli and Adam Gaudette on the power play, Zack Ostapchuk, then Eric Pohlkamp's first NHL goal to tie it at 4 in the third. Dmitry Orlov put the Sharks ahead with 5:43 left and finished with four points; Barrett Hayton tied it again on the power play two minutes later. In the shootout Vincent Trocheck and Macklin Celebrini traded goals before Mason Marchment won it in the fifth round. Karel Vejmelka gave up five on 21 shots (Andre Tourigny said afterward 'Vej has to be better'), and Yaroslav Askarov made 27 saves. Andrew Peeke fought Ty Dellandrea and then Gaudette. Utah's defense went the full 65 minutes without showing up, a real commitment to the bit.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI6ANA2Final: NYI 6, ANA 2

Simon Holmstrom picked a good night for his first career hat trick: the Islanders beat Anaheim 6-2, and Mathew Barzal got an assist on Ben Hutton's goal 1:55 into his season debut. Bo Horvat scored on the power play, Holmstrom scored twice in 5:27 of the second, Mitchell Chaffee made it 5-1, and Holmstrom finished the job early in the third. Matthew Schaefer had three assists, because apparently the 19-year-old is also the Isles' playmaker now. Semyon Varlamov stopped 26 of 28; Lukas Dostal stayed in for all 60 minutes and six goals on 25 shots, which is the kind of loyalty usually reserved for a bad contract. Nikita Nesterenko and Cutter Gauthier (his 17th) scored for the Ducks. The Ducks were down 5-1 before the game was half over, then left their goalie out there to absorb a sixth: that's not goaltending support, that's a dare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY3LAK2Final: CGY 3, LAK 2

Calgary opened its road trip with a 3-2 win in Los Angeles, and the Kings helped. Morgan Frost scored early in the second off a Cody Ceci turnover, and Ceci watched the third period from the bench. Joel Armia tied it at 6:21 of the third, Matvei Gridin answered five minutes later for the winner, and Yegor Sharangovich hit the empty net with 1:14 left. Mats Zuccarello's first of the season with the goalie pulled made it close 18 seconds later. Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 31; Anton Forsberg 21 of 23. The Kings are 5-11-2, level with Chicago at 12 points and ahead of only Vancouver, a Hollywood ending nobody in LA wanted to see.

Saturday, November 14

Game recap

NYR5VAN1Final: NYR 5, VAN 1

Vancouver hung around for a period, which at this point counts as a moral victory. Elias Pettersson opened the scoring at 12:13 of the first, Gabe Perreault answered before intermission, and then the second period happened: four Rangers goals in 7:49. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on the power play, Glenn Gawdin got his first NHL goal unassisted, Alexis Lafrenière buried his 10th, and Gawdin added his second just 56 seconds later. A guy who played 7:59 had two goals; the entire Canucks lineup had one. J.T. Miller set up two against his old team, Dylan Garand stopped 27 of 28, and Leevi Meriläinen made 26 saves on 31. New York is 12-8-1. Vancouver is 3-17-1 with seven straight losses, and the only thing the Canucks are building right now is a lottery ticket.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3VGK2SOFinal: NSH 3, VGK 2 SO

Vegas threw 42 shots at Juuse Saros and got two past him, so naturally this one needed a shootout. Ryan O'Reilly scored at 7:56 of the first, Victor Olofsson tied it, and Rasmus Andersson put Vegas ahead in the second. O'Reilly tied it again at 9:44 of the third, his second of the night and ninth of the season, and overtime settled nothing. In the shootout Trevor Connelly scored for Vegas, Filip Forsberg answered, Jack Eichel was stopped and Roman Josi ended it, after playing 31:40 and apparently still having legs. Saros made 40 saves; Adin Hill made 30 on 32. Nashville has won seven straight and is 11-4-5. Vegas outshot its guests by 10 and went home with one point, which in that town is called breaking even and still feels like losing.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friday, November 13

Game recap

CAR4SEA1Final: CAR 4, SEA 1

The NHL flew Seattle across an ocean to play a home game in Helsinki, and the Kraken honored the occasion with 13 shots, roughly what Carolina's fourth line puts up on a slow Tuesday. Nikolaj Ehlers opened the scoring at 11:44 of the first, Sebastian Aho added a power-play goal 66 seconds later, and Juuso Välimäki made it 3-0 in the second. Aho finished the job with his 12th of the year in the third, while K'Andre Miller and Logan Stankoven had two assists each. Brandon Bussi stopped 12 of 13, which barely counts as working, and Frederick Gaudreau spoiled the shutout with 6:45 left. Philipp Grubauer made 26 saves on 30 shots. The Canes are 15-3-2, tied with Minnesota for the league lead at 32 points. The two teams do it again Saturday in Finland, so Seattle gets one more shot at finding the Carolina net, or failing that, some decent sightseeing.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL5BOS2Final: MTL 5, BOS 2

Boston's four-game win streak lasted exactly as long as it took Montreal to walk into TD Garden. The Habs scored the first five goals: Kirby Dach at 2:34, Josh Anderson in the first, then Jake Evans, an unassisted Cole Caufield (his 12th) and Phillip Danault in the second. Jeremy Swayman was pulled after four goals on 17 shots, and Michael DiPietro stopped 13 of 14 in relief, which is the kind of relief that comes after the house has already burned down. Casey Mittelstadt scored twice for Boston, late in the second and 53 seconds into the third, with Elias Lindholm assisting both, but Jacob Fowler shut the door with 30 saves on 32 shots. Montreal is 12-3-4, tied with Tampa Bay for the Atlantic lead at 28 points, and 8-0-2 in its last 10. That's the kind of run Bruins fans used to think was their birthright, and now they get to watch it in the other sweater.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5TOR2Final: MIN 5, TOR 2

Matt Boldy brought his own hat to Scotiabank Arena and left with everyone else's. Boldy opened the scoring late in the first, tied it on the power play in the second and put Minnesota ahead for good 3:59 into the third, a hat trick with Kirill Kaprizov assisting the first two. In between, Toronto actually led: Auston Matthews scored his 12th and Zack MacEwen made it 2-1 early in the second, a lead that lasted a little under three minutes. Michael McCarron added a fourth and Danila Yurov hit the empty net, giving Kaprizov his third assist. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves on 28 shots; Anthony Stolarz stopped 21 of 25. The Wild are 14-3-4 and tied for the league lead at 32 points. The Leafs are 8-11-2, have lost five straight and are 3-7-0 in their last 10, and somewhere in Toronto a man is already pricing out April tee times.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL3OTT4OTFinal: COL 3, OTT 4 OT

Shane Pinto started it and Shane Pinto finished it. He scored unassisted 7:11 in, Tim Stützle made it 2-0 later in the first, and Pinto won it alone again 2:08 into overtime. The middle was all Colorado, which played much of the night without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar after both left in the second period with lower-body injuries. Artturi Lehkonen scored his 14th on the power play, Parker Kelly scored shorthanded early in the third, and Gabriel Landeskog put the Avalanche ahead 3-2 on another power play at 10:03. Drake Batherson tied it with 3:56 left. Linus Ullmark made 26 saves on 29 shots; Scott Wedgewood stopped 22 of 26. The Senators are 12-6-2 and fourth in the Atlantic. Colorado takes a point to Montreal for Saturday, plus a lesson: a one-goal lead with ten minutes left is a suggestion, not a plan.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH2NJD5Final: WSH 2, NJD 5

Washington led in the second period, which in hindsight was just the Devils letting them hold it for a minute. Evan Rodrigues scored on the power play 2:20 in, Ryan Leonard answered on one of his own, and Pierre-Luc Dubois put the Capitals up 2-1 early in the second. That lasted 7:40. Lenni Hameenaho tied it with his first of the season, Vladislav Kolyachonok scored his first for the go-ahead goal 6:27 into the third, Stefan Noesen added one late, and Jack Hughes hit the empty net for his 10th. Rodrigues finished with a goal and an assist. Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves on 28 shots; Logan Thompson stopped 24 of 28. New Jersey is 14-6-0 and 8-2-0 in its last 10, second in the Metropolitan. The Capitals are 10-7-0 with 67 games left, tied for the most in the league, which is a lot of hockey for a team that couldn't keep a lead for eight minutes.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL3CBJ1Final: TBL 3, CBJ 1

Tampa Bay showed up in Columbus without Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak and still looked like the team with the plan. Brandon Hagel scored 2:57 in, Matthew Knies tied it on a Columbus power play, and then the two teams fought twice in two seconds: Mathieu Olivier with Scott Sabourin and Ryan Lomberg with Jeffrey Viel, 12:22 and 12:24 of the first. After that the Lightning went back to hockey. Jake Guentzel scored his 11th 1:06 into the third and Hagel added his 13th, with Nikita Kucherov assisting both of Hagel's goals. Dennis Hildeby stopped 28 of 29; Jet Greaves made 25 saves on 28 shots. Sean Monahan left late in the second with an upper-body injury. The Lightning are 13-4-2 and first in the Atlantic. Columbus is 7-10-0, last in the Metropolitan and on a three-game skid, and its best shift of the night was a two-second stretch with the gloves off.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET4FLA5Final: DET 4, FLA 5

Detroit led Florida 4-1 in the second period, and if you've watched the Red Wings lately you already know how this ends. J.T. Compher, Andreas Englund, Lucas Raymond and Marco Kasper (his first of the year) built the lead after Sam Reinhart's opener. Then Gustav Forsling scored with 18 seconds left in the second, Anton Lundell scored early in the third, Lars Eller tied it at 16:29, and Lundell won it 51 seconds later, with both Tkachuks assisting. Carter Verhaeghe had three assists. Akira Schmid made 24 saves on 28 shots; John Gibson stopped 24 of 29. Alex DeBrincat and Sam Bennett dropped the gloves in the second. The Panthers are 11-7-2 and have won two straight. The Red Wings are 7-10-3 and have lost five in a row, and blowing a three-goal lead in under 18 minutes is a fresh way to do it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF2CHI3OTFinal: BUF 2, CHI 3 OT

Buffalo went to Chicago, the softest landing spot in the Central, and still flew home with a loss. Owen Power opened the scoring, Frank Nazar answered on the power play with Connor Bedard assisting, and Tage Thompson's 12th, also on the power play, put the Sabres back up 2-1 after one. Then nobody scored for more than a period until Nazar tied it 8:22 into the third, and Ryan Donato won it 3:12 into overtime, set up by Anton Frondell and Sam Rinzel, who had two assists. Spencer Knight stopped 21 of 23; Alex Lyon made 22 saves on 25 shots. Chicago is still last in the Central at 5-13-1, but it has a win streak now, all one game of it. The Sabres are 8-7-4 and -13, and losing in overtime to the Blackhawks is one point in the standings and a new low everywhere else.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG8DAL3Final: WPG 8, DAL 3

Dallas led 2-0 after one and 3-2 halfway through the game, and then Winnipeg scored the last six goals like it was running a drill. Arttu Hyry and Roope Hintz gave the Stars the early lead, Dylan Samberg and Mark Scheifele scored unassisted to tie it, and David Perron's first of the season put Dallas back ahead. After that: Dawson Mercer, a Scheifele power-play goal and Mercer again with nine seconds left in the second, then Kyle Connor (his 16th) a minute into the third, which ended Jake Oettinger's night at six goals on 27 shots. Gabriel Vilardi and Cole Koepke scored 14 seconds apart late, and Casey DeSmith stopped one of three. Scheifele, Connor and Vilardi each had three points; Stuart Skinner made 30 saves on 33 shots. The Jets have won five straight. The Stars held a players-only meeting afterward, which is what you do when eight goals on home ice needs a closed door.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL1UTA0SOFinal: STL 1, UTA 0 SO

Sixty-five minutes, zero goals, and the most exciting thing in regulation was Liam O'Brien and Ross Johnston fighting 1:56 in. Joel Hofer stopped all 29 Utah shots and Karel Vejmelka stopped all 22 from St. Louis, so the night went to a shootout that needed eight rounds. Vincent Trocheck and Jake Neighbours scored in the first, the next ten shooters all missed, then Michael Carcone and Jimmy Snuggerud traded goals in the seventh. Barrett Hayton was stopped in the eighth, and Connor McMichael ended it. The Blues are 9-8-2 and have won two straight. The Mammoth are 10-8-2 and 3-5-2 in their last 10, and they went two for eight in the shootout on the way to being shut out at home. Utah's offense is going the way of its mascot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI5LAK2Final: NYI 5, LAK 2

The Islanders ended a four-game winless streak in Los Angeles, and Matthew Schaefer marked his 100th NHL game with a power-play goal, his sixth, to put them ahead 2-1 in the first. Brayden Schenn opened the scoring and finished with a goal and two assists, Victor Eklund made it 3-1 in the second, and Simon Holmstrom scored unassisted 39 seconds into the third before setting up Bo Horvat's empty-netter. Trevor Moore and Quinton Byfield, on a power play set up by Artemi Panarin and Kevin Fiala, scored for the Kings. Tony DeAngelo and Corey Perry fought in the second. Ilya Sorokin made 26 saves on 28 shots; Darcy Kuemper stopped 16 of 20. The Islanders are 8-6-4. The Kings are 5-10-2, have lost three straight and sit seventh in the Pacific, and the only thing keeping them out of the basement is Vancouver.

Thursday, November 12

Game recap

TBL8BUF3Final: TBL 8, BUF 3

Buffalo spent 20 minutes doing the hard part, climbing out of a 4-0 hole with three goals in 4:39 from Josh Doan, Jason Zucker and Tage Thompson to make it 4-3 early in the third. Then Nikita Kucherov decided the comeback had gone on long enough. He scored three straight, the last on the power play, for a natural hat trick inside 13 minutes, and Brandon Hagel's second of the night made it 8-3. John Carlson had a goal and four assists to reach 800 career points, Scott Sabourin and Yanni Gourde scored their first goals of the season, and Sam O'Reilly got his first NHL point in his debut. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 28 saves. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 9 of 14 and got the hook; Colten Ellis came in and stopped 5 of 8, which is not the spark Lindy Ruff ordered. Tampa is 12-4-2. The Sabres get on a plane to Chicago, and the fans get the view they know best: hope for half an hour, then the bill.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR3CGY1Final: NYR 3, CGY 1

Mika Zibanejad did all the heavy lifting in Calgary, scoring 59 seconds into the second and again on the power play at 10:52 for a 2-0 Rangers lead. Adam Klapka got one back on a Flames power play with 12:19 left, and that was the last time a Calgary shot got anywhere: Joonas Korpisalo made 29 saves on 30, and Tye Kartye put one into the empty net with seven seconds to go. Glenn Gawdin made his Rangers debut at fourth-line center, his first NHL game since March 2024, which is a nice story the Flames will be reading about from below .500. Devin Cooley stopped 21 of 23. New York is 11-8-1 with four wins in five. Calgary is 8-10-1 and finished its homestand 1-1-1: put 30 shots on net, scored one, and went home. That's the Flames' offense in a sentence, and it's a short sentence.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI2EDM3OTFinal: PHI 2, EDM 3 OT

Philadelphia did the brave thing. Down 2-0 on a pair from Zach Hyman (one on the power play, set up by Connor McDavid), the Flyers got a power-play goal from Tyson Foerster and a tying shot from Travis Sanheim with 8:18 left, then forced overtime, where they lasted 47 seconds. Leon Draisaitl found Evan Bouchard, and Bouchard ended it. McDavid's assist ran his point streak to all 20 games of the season, the second straight year he's done it. Tristan Jarry made 30 saves on 32 and Dan Vladar stopped 21 of 24. Edmonton is 14-3-3 with three straight wins. The Flyers are 5-10-6, and six of those are overtime or shootout losses: plenty of points, none of the joy. Philly's on its way to the most expensive participation trophy in hockey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA3VGK5Final: UTA 3, VGK 5

Vegas put Utah on the clock 2:15 in when Jack Eichel scored on the power play, and the Golden Knights' special teams never really let go. Lawson Crouse tied it, Victor Olofsson scored on another power play early in the second, and Ivan Barbashev scored twice in 3:25 for a 4-1 lead. Jack McBain and Dmitri Simashev made it 4-3 with 10:53 left, and Brett Howden answered 72 seconds later. Olofsson had a goal and two assists, Mitch Marner three assists, and Carter Hart only had to stop 14 of 17, because Utah could only find 17 shots all night. Sebastian Cossa made 23 saves on 28. Vegas is 13-5-2 with four straight wins. The Mammoth are 10-8-1 with three straight losses, and 17 shots in a game you trail all night isn't a comeback plan. It's a bus schedule.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH4ANA2Final: NSH 4, ANA 2

The hottest offense in hockey ran into the hottest team in hockey, and it was Anaheim that blinked. Cutter Gauthier scored his 16th of the season for a 1-0 Ducks lead and got to enjoy it for 21 seconds before Jayden Struble tied it. Nils Hoglander put Nashville ahead in the second, Shane Wright scored his first goal as a Predator in the third and added two assists, and after Mikael Granlund made it 3-2, Steven Stamkos scored his 11th with under four minutes left. Roman Josi had two assists to reach 800 career points. Justus Annunen made 27 saves on 29, and Laurent Brossoit stopped 18 of 22. Nashville is 10-4-5 with six straight wins. The Ducks are 10-8-1: their five-game win streak is over, and so is a run of eight straight games with five or more goals. Turns out the Ducks' scoring was a rental, and the lease was up in Nashville.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT3SJS2SOFinal: PIT 3, SJS 2 SO

Pittsburgh held a 2-0 lead with nine minutes to go, which in 2026 is when the Penguins start getting nervous. Samuel Girard scored in the first and Ben Kindel added a power-play goal early in the third. Then Macklin Celebrini scored at 11:32 and set up Mason Marchment's tying goal at 15:49, giving Celebrini 200 career points. Overtime solved nothing, so it went to a shootout, where Kindel scored on the first attempt and Sergei Murashov stopped Celebrini, Ivar Stenberg and Will Smith. Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell both missed, so it's a good thing the kid was there. Murashov made 34 saves on 36 in regulation and OT, and Yaroslav Askarov made 33 on 35. Pittsburgh is 7-10-2. San Jose is 8-11-2 and came back from two down to lose anyway: the Sharks found a new way to go home with one point, and their fans have collected every version of that.

Wednesday, November 11

Game recap

COL6TOR3Final: COL 6, TOR 3

Toronto finally remembered how to score, which only made it more painful when Colorado scored more. Darren Raddysh put the Leafs up 3:33 in, Easton Cowan cut it to 3-2 late in the second, and Jack Roslovic tied it 3-3 early in the third. Then Gabriel Landeskog took the tie away 51 seconds later for his second goal of the night, Artturi Lehkonen made it 5-3 with 2:45 left and Martin Necas hit the empty net 15 seconds after that. Cale Makar had two assists in 23:23, Devon Toews had a goal and an assist, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 28 of 31. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 22 of 27. That's four straight losses and 8-10-2 for the Leafs, who keep finding new ways to make a hot start feel like a rumor from someone else's season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN2MTL1OTFinal: MIN 2, MTL 1 OT

Two of the best teams in hockey played 42 minutes of scoreless chess before anybody remembered the nets were there. Bobby Brink finally broke it 2:53 into the third, unassisted, for his second of the year, and Minnesota nearly closed it out until Nick Suzuki tied it with 1:38 left, six-on-five with Jacob Fowler on the bench. Overtime lasted 21 seconds: Kirill Kaprizov buried a power-play winner from Matt Boldy and Quinn Hughes, his 17th goal, with Hughes logging 29:28 like a man paid by the minute. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 27 of 28; Fowler stopped 22 of 24. The Wild are 13-3-4 with 30 points. Montreal goes home with the loser point at 11-3-4, which Habs fans will gladly point out is one more than Toronto got last night.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH3OTT2OTFinal: WSH 3, OTT 2 OT

Washington took 17 shots all night and still left Ottawa with two points, which is the kind of efficiency usually reserved for tax accountants. Matt Roy scored 35 seconds in, his first of the season, before Ottawa took over: Ridly Greig tied it and Hayden Hodgson, on 6:35 of ice time, put the Senators ahead late in the second, both set up by Thomas Chabot. Pierre-Luc Dubois tied it 2-2 at 12:31 of the third, and Cole Hutson won it 1:14 into overtime from Alex Ovechkin and Dylan Strome, his fifth goal to go with an assist. Logan Thompson stopped 24 of 26. Samuel Ersson stopped 14 of 17, and Ottawa (11-6-2) outshot the Capitals 26-17 and still lost, which takes real commitment.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD2WPG4Final: NJD 2, WPG 4

The Jets went nine games without a win, then woke up and decided to take everyone's lunch money. Winnipeg ended New Jersey's five-game win streak for its own fourth straight win, with Kyle Connor and Dawson Mercer scoring twice each. Mercer opened it in the first, and Connor's power-play goal made it 2-0. The Devils tied it 44 seconds apart early in the second on goals by Jesper Bratt and Cody Glass, but Mercer's power-play goal at 11:58 of the third put Winnipeg back ahead, and Connor's empty-netter, his 15th, closed it. Cole Perfetti had two assists, and Nico Daws stopped 19 of 21 on a night New Jersey managed only 21 shots. Jake Allen stopped 21 of 24. The Devils' streak ran on overtime and shootouts for weeks; Winnipeg simply refused to let this one get that far.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA4CBJ1Final: FLA 4, CBJ 1

Columbus threw 38 shots at Jacob Markstrom and got back exactly one goal, which is the hockey version of sending 38 job applications and landing one interview. Markstrom stopped 37 of them, and Florida snapped a two-game skid. Sam Bennett scored twice, the first on the power play early in the second, and Lars Eller made it 2-0 a little over two minutes later. Ivan Provorov got Columbus on the board with 19 seconds left in the second, but Bennett answered in the third and Sam Reinhart hit the empty net for his 10th. Aaron Ekblad and Anton Lundell had two assists each. Cam Talbot stopped 24 of 27. The Blue Jackets are 7-9-0 and shooting like every puck owes them money and none of them plan to pay.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET2STL3Final: DET 2, STL 3

St. Louis finally won a hockey game, and of course it was Detroit that let it happen. Andrew Copp gave the Red Wings a 1-0 lead with 13 seconds left in the first, and Detroit held it for all of 37 seconds into the second before Pius Suter tied it; Justin Barron made it 2-1 two minutes later. Jimmy Snuggerud scored his 10th with 4:02 left, and Moritz Seider's first of the season, six-on-five with 1:14 to go, only made it close. Joel Hofer stopped 30 of 32, John Gibson 30 of 33, and Ross Johnston and Andreas Englund fought in the second. It's the Blues' first win in four games and their second over Detroit in 10 days. The Red Wings have lost four straight, and the Larkin standoff is still the most suspense in Hockeytown.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3LAK0Final: NSH 3, LAK 0

The Kings went 108 straight regular-season games without getting shut out, then met Juuse Saros. He stopped all 28 shots and Nashville opened its West Coast trip with a fifth straight win. Filip Forsberg did the scoring, early in the first and midway through the second, both set up by Nils Hoglander, and Adam Wilsby added an unassisted empty-netter for his first of the season. Adam Edstrom and Andre Lee fought in the second, which was about as close as LA came to a goal. Anton Forsberg stopped 27 of 29 for the Kings. Nashville is 9-4-5 and has quietly become a problem. Los Angeles is 5-9-2, which in Hollywood they'll call a slow opening weekend right up until it's April.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Tuesday, November 10

Game recap

NYR1EDM3Final: NYR 1, EDM 3

Connor McDavid's assist streak finally died at 18 games, so he did the only reasonable thing and scored instead. Dylan Garand's pass bounced off the back of his own net, McDavid said thank you 6:42 in, and the season-opening point streak reached 19, the longest since Dany Heatley's in 2005. Leon Draisaitl made it 2-0 early in the second, Jaroslav Chmelar answered shorthanded for New York, and then Draisaitl closed it with another shorthanded goal, into the empty net with 1:13 left. Devon Levi stopped 28 of 29 to go 8-1-0, Garand made 17 saves and, technically, one assist. Edmonton is 13-3-3. The Rangers outshot the Oilers 29-20 and still left Rogers Place with one goal and a reminder that the best player in the world will happily take whatever you hand him, even the puck off your own net.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI3VAN1Final: PHI 3, VAN 1

Michael Bunting went from healthy scratch to hero in 2:03, scoring his first goal as a Flyer before most of Rogers Arena had found its seats. Travis Konecny made it 2-0 on the power play in the second, which for the league's lowest-scoring offense counts as a scoring explosion. Jonathan Lekkerimäki got one back on a Vancouver power play with 7:16 left, then Travis Sanheim ended it shorthanded into the empty net. Joseph Woll stopped 18 of 19, Leevi Meriläinen 14 of 16, and the two teams combined for 36 shots, the hockey equivalent of a group project where nobody wants to present. David Jiricek played 13:23 after eight straight scratches. Philadelphia (5-10-5) ends a three-game winless run. Vancouver loses a sixth straight and falls to 3-16-1: when the Flyers come to your building and look like the offense, it's time to check the standings, and then look away.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI2SJS3SOFinal: NYI 2, SJS 3 SO

Sixteen shooters, eight rounds, and Ivar Stenberg finally put everybody out of their misery. The Sharks came from behind twice: Ben Hutton scored his first goal as an Islander and Victor Eklund added one on the power play, and Stenberg and Tyler Toffoli answered both times. Then nobody scored for the last 33 minutes of hockey, and the first 15 shootout attempts went nowhere either. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 30 of 32 and all eight Islanders shooters; Ilya Sorokin made 37 saves on 39 shots and deserved better. The second period ended with a four-man scrap, Barclay Goodrow and Ty Dellandrea against Mitchell Chaffee and Kyle MacLean, the liveliest anyone looked after Toffoli's tying goal. San Jose ends a five-game skid. The Islanders have lost four straight (0-2-2) and went 0-for-8 in the shootout: a team that can't score in a skills competition is just a very well-dressed defensive clinic.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, November 9

Game recap

FLA1BOS4Final: FLA 1, BOS 4

Two seconds. That's how long it took for Nikita Zadorov and Brady Tkachuk to drop the gloves, and Garnet Hathaway and Mark Kastelic had their own go before the 7-minute mark, so nobody can say this one lacked a pulse. Boston then did the actual hockey: Elias Lindholm at 4:50, Michael Eyssimont's first of the year at 6:11 and Morgan Geekie on the power play at 15:59 made it 3-0 inside 16 minutes. Carter Verhaeghe answered on a Florida power play before the first intermission, and that was the end of the Panthers' fun. JJ Peterka buried one 58 seconds into the third off Pastrnak and Zacha, who had two assists apiece. Jeremy Swayman stopped 40 of 41, Jacob Markstrom 32 of 36. The Bruins have won four straight and sit first in the Atlantic. The Panthers put 41 shots on net and lost by three, which is a lot of work for a one-goal paycheck.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK4BUF1Final: VGK 4, BUF 1

Forty minutes of nothing, then Mitch Marner went and did it while Vegas was a man down: an unassisted shorthanded goal at 12:17 of the second, which is the kind of hospitality Buffalo usually saves for its own power play. Jack Eichel made it 2-0 86 seconds later off Ivan Barbashev. Beck Malenstyn got the Sabres on the board early in the third with his first of the season, and Tomas Hertl promptly ended the suspense with two goals in barely four minutes, the second with 10:00 left. Adin Hill stopped 28 of 29; Colten Ellis saw 26 and let in four. Barbashev had two assists, Marner a goal and one, and the Golden Knights have won three straight on this trip. The Sabres outshot Vegas 29-26 and still never led, so at least the Buffalo tradition of losing with good possession numbers is safe.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL3WPG4Final: TBL 3, WPG 4

Winnipeg spent 50 minutes building a 3-0 lead, Tampa Bay spent four minutes erasing it, and then Mark Scheifele won it on a power play with two seconds left. Cole Perfetti (power play), Morgan Barron and Brayden Yager (power play, his first of the season) put the Jets up three. Then Brandon Hagel scored at 10:22 of the third and Pontus Holmberg scored twice 26 seconds apart, at 14:01 and 14:27, to tie it. A Tampa Bay penalty late gave the Jets one more power play, and Scheifele finished it at 19:58 off Perfetti and Gabriel Vilardi. Stuart Skinner stopped 18 of 21, Andrei Vasilevskiy 21 of 25. Yanni Gourde made his season debut for Tampa, and Brayden Point left in the first. Three straight wins for a team that just went nine without one. The Lightning came all the way back and then gave it away with the clock almost out, which is a very Florida way to spend a Sunday.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD4TOR0Final: NJD 4, TOR 0

Connor Hellebuyck came to Toronto and turned out the lights: 23 saves, 23 stops, a shutout for the new guy in a Devils sweater. Timo Meier did the scoring, twice in the second, at 8:28 off Nico Hischier and at 12:44 off Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt. Hischier added a power-play goal in the third, Hughes and Bratt picked up their second assists of the night, and Connor Brown hit the empty net. New Jersey did it with 11 forwards and seven defensemen, and it was still never close. Anthony Stolarz stopped 25 of 28 and deserved better company. That's five straight wins for the Devils and 9-1-0 in their last 10. The Leafs have lost three in a row, scored two goals in the last two games, and got shut out at home on a Sunday night, which is still the most reliable thing Toronto produces in November.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI3CGY4OTFinal: PHI 3, CGY 4 OT

Philadelphia led this game three separate times and still flew home with one point, which is the most Flyers sentence of the week. Denver Barkey, Noel Acciari and Owen Tippett (power play) each gave them a lead; Zayne Parekh and Zach Whitecloud, two Calgary defensemen, kept answering. Then Joel Farabee tied it with a shorthanded goal at 8:27 of the third, the Flames killing a penalty and scoring on it at the same time. Matt Coronato won it 4:08 into overtime off Matvei Gridin and Simon Nemec. Devin Cooley made 32 saves on 35 shots, and Dan Vladar 22 on 26 at the other end. The Flames have won two of their last four. The Flyers score the fewest goals in the league, found three in Calgary, and still couldn't hold any of them, like a guy who finally gets paid and leaves his wallet on the bus.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT2ANA5Final: PIT 2, ANA 5

Cutter Gauthier had the kind of night that gets hats thrown on the ice: three goals and an assist, up to 15 on the season, one behind the league lead. Mikael Granlund scored a power-play goal and set up three more, Gauthier's power-play goal and even-strength goal made it 3-0 midway through the second, and Tristan Luneau added a fourth on the power play. Pittsburgh got two late, both 6-on-5 with the goalie pulled on a power play (Kris Letang's first of the year, then Rickard Rakell), and Gauthier ended it into the empty net with 34 seconds left. Laurent Brossoit stopped 31 of 33 and is 4-0 since his recall; Arturs Silovs stopped 20 of 24. Anaheim has won five straight. The Penguins have lost four of five, and Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin are spending another fall setting up garbage-time goals.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, November 8

Game recap

FLA3WSH4Final: FLA 3, WSH 4

Family night in Washington went to the Capitals, 4-3, and the Tkachuk brothers did everything they could to spoil it. Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the first period, both set up by Matthew, the second on the power play, for a 2-1 Florida lead. Then the Panthers stopped scoring and Washington didn't. Alex Tuch tied it with his 11th, unassisted, early in the second; Aliaksei Protas put the Caps ahead, and Pierre-Luc Dubois made it 4-2 early in the third, the two of them setting each other up like a buddy-cop movie. Jack St. Ivany had opened the scoring 2:21 in, also unassisted, because apparently nobody in red needed help. Tom Wilson's night lasted 2:13 and ended with 15 penalty minutes for boarding Sandis Vilmanis. Sam Bennett got one back with 47 seconds left and the goalie pulled. Logan Thompson made 27 saves, Akira Schmid 27 on 31. Matthew Tkachuk had three assists and still went home with nothing to show for them.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL1NSH3Final: STL 1, NSH 3

Nashville beat St. Louis 3-1, and Juuse Saros was the reason: 25 saves on 26 shots, with the only goal going in on a Blues power play. Jimmy Snuggerud scored that one, his ninth, midway through the first. Steven Stamkos answered on a Predators power play three minutes later for his 10th, and Ross Colton's goal at 9:02 of the second, set up by Jack Drury and Roman Josi, turned out to be the winner. Nick Perbix finished it into an empty net with 1:29 left. Joel Hofer was good at the other end, 26 saves on 28, which is the kind of night Blues goalies keep having: good enough to lose by two. Nashville is 8-4-5 and finally winning in regulation. St. Louis is 7-8-2, and its offense showed up for one power play and then went looking for the parking lot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR4SEA3Final: NYR 4, SEA 3

The Rangers beat Seattle 4-3, which reads a lot closer than it was for 40 minutes. Gabe Perreault scored 95 seconds in, Tye Kartye added a power-play goal and Jaroslav Chmelar scored his first of the season, and Joey Daccord was on the bench after three goals on 10 shots in 13:53. Pavel Dorofeyev made it 4-0 in the second off Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière. Then the Kraken remembered they're a hockey team: Kaapo Kakko, Jordan Eberle on the power play and Vince Dunn at 15:02 of the third pulled them within one. Joonas Korpisalo held the rest, 25 saves on 28. Philipp Grubauer stopped 15 of 16 in relief. Adam Fox picked up his 20th assist in 18 games, faster than any Rangers defenseman ever, Brian Leetch included. New York is 10-7-1. Seattle is 9-6-1 and has now perfected the art of the third-period comeback that starts about 20 minutes too late.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL4TOR2Final: MTL 4, TOR 2

Montreal won 4-2 in Toronto, and the Leafs' coach spent part of it teaching a rookie a lesson in front of the home crowd. Alex Newhook scored twice in the first period for a 2-0 lead. In the second, Chris Kreider picked off Gavin McKenna's pass and scored on a breakaway for 3-0, and Hiller sat McKenna for the rest of the period. To his credit, McKenna came back and scored in the third, 55 seconds after William Nylander's power-play goal, and suddenly it was 3-2. Zachary Bolduc answered on the power play at 12:15 to end the drama. Jacob Fowler made 26 saves on 28; Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 24 of 28. The Canadiens are 11-3-3 and look like they're having fun. The Leafs are 8-8-2 with four regulation losses in five games, which in Toronto counts as a five-alarm fire and a full week of radio.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA2OTT4Final: UTA 2, OTT 4

Ottawa beat Utah 4-2 with a late winner, and Samuel Ersson was the best player on the ice: 30 saves on 32 shots. Fabian Zetterlund put the Senators ahead on a first-period power play, Clayton Keller tied it four minutes later, and the game sat there until the third. Michael Amadio scored at 6:29, Barrett Hayton tied it again at 9:53 off Keller, and then Nick Cousins, of all people, scored the winner with 2:18 left, from Thomas Chabot and Shane Pinto. Pinto added the empty-netter at 19:44. Karel Vejmelka made 17 saves on 20. Ottawa is 11-6-1. Utah is 10-7-1 and outshot the Senators 32-21, which means the Mammoth did the heavy lifting all night and still got stuck with the bill.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD5NYI4OTFinal: NJD 5, NYI 4 OT

New Jersey beat the Islanders 5-4 in overtime after trailing 4-2 midway through the game, and the Islanders can't say they weren't warned: the Devils outshot them 50-23. Ilya Sorokin made 45 saves and still lost, which is about the cruelest thing that can happen to a goalie. Anthony Duclair, Matthew Schaefer, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund scored for New York; Evan Rodrigues and Declan Chisholm kept New Jersey close. In the third, Luke Evangelista scored at 6:08 and Dougie Hamilton tied it on the power play at 13:42. Then Jack Hughes ended it 1:18 into overtime, assisted by his brother Luke. Jake Allen made 19 saves on 23 with Connor Hellebuyck getting the night off. The Devils are 12-5-0. The Islanders are 7-6-3 and spent 61 minutes proving that two-goal leads are just a suggestion.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI2CAR9Final: CHI 2, CAR 9

Carolina beat Chicago 9-2, and it was 7-0 after two periods, so the third was mostly paperwork. Jordan Martinook scored twice in the first, Andrei Svechnikov scored twice overall, and Seth Jarvis, Jackson Blake, Sebastian Aho, Alexander Nikishin and Shayne Gostisbehere all joined in. Nine goals tied the Hurricanes' record for a game since they left Hartford. Spencer Knight was pulled after six goals on 17 shots; Arvid Soderblom gave up three more on 16. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves and has won 11 of his first 12 starts, something only 10 other goalies have done. Connor Bedard set up Roman Kantserov and scored himself in the third, long after it mattered. The Hurricanes are 14-3-2. The Blackhawks are 4-13-1 after six straight losses and held a players-only meeting afterward. Chicago keeps buying the rebuild, and the house keeps winning.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3DAL4Final: SJS 3, DAL 4

Dallas beat San Jose 4-3, and three power-play goals did it. Michael Misa scored first for the Sharks, then Roope Hintz on the power play, Jamie Benn at even strength and Jason Robertson on another power play made it 3-1 Dallas in the first. Benn's goal was his 999th career point, so Dallas fans get to do this all over again. Ivar Stenberg pulled San Jose within one early in the second, Thomas Harley's power-play one-timer made it 4-2, and Will Smith answered on a Sharks power play 2:32 later. Nobody scored in the third. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves on 23, Alex Nedeljkovic 26 on 30. Macklin Celebrini had three assists. The Stars are 10-5-2. The Sharks are 7-11-1, with a penalty kill that let in three goals on a night they lost by one, which is how you lose a hockey game while doing everything else right.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL4MIN3OTFinal: TBL 4, MIN 3 OT

Tampa Bay was down 3-1 in Minnesota with about 13 minutes left and won 4-3 in overtime, with the winner scored by the guy who reportedly wants out of town. Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov scored early for the Wild, Jake Guentzel answered on a second-period power play, and Shabanov made it 3-1 at 6:49 of the third. Then Guentzel scored again at 13:44, Charle-Edouard D'Astous tied it at 16:29 with the goalie pulled on a power play, and Nikita Kucherov ended it 3:23 into overtime on another power play. So much for a quiet farewell tour. Dennis Hildeby made 19 saves on 22; Calvin Pickard stopped 30 of 34. Marcus Foligno and Scott Sabourin fought in the first. Tampa is 11-3-2 and plays in Winnipeg tonight. Minnesota is 12-3-4, still first in the Central, and found out a two-goal lead in the third doesn't come with a warranty.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET0COL4Final: DET 0, COL 4

Colorado shut out Detroit 4-0, and Mackenzie Blackwood didn't have to do anything fancy: 27 saves, all of them, against a Red Wings team that never found the net. Martin Necas and Nathan MacKinnon scored on power plays 2:44 apart in the second period, Necas added another at 7:15 of the third, and Cale Makar finished it on yet another power play at 9:45, three goals with the extra man in all. Necas finished with four points, Makar with three and MacKinnon with a goal and two assists. Gabriel Landeskog and Moritz Seider fought in the third, which was the most success Detroit had all night. Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves on 29. The Avalanche are 10-6-2. The Red Wings are 7-8-3, with their captain suspended and the team still looking for him in its offense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT5LAK2Final: PIT 5, LAK 2

Pittsburgh won 5-2 in Los Angeles, and Sidney Crosby made some history in the building where Marcel Dionne's jersey hangs. Crosby scored twice, the second into an empty net, to pass Dionne for sixth on the NHL's career points list. Tommy Novak got things going with two goals in the first 5:10. Corey Perry got one back for the Kings, Egor Chinakhov scored on the power play, and Alex Laferriere made it 3-2 on a Kings power play early in the second, but Crosby's first goal, late in the second, put it away. Evgeni Malkin had three assists. Sergei Murashov made 26 saves on 28 for his first win of the season; Darcy Kuemper stopped 14 of 18. The Penguins are 6-9-2 and in Anaheim tonight. The Kings are 5-8-2 and just watched a 39-year-old pass a franchise icon on their own ice, which is a lot to ask of a fan base already paying for this roster.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2EDM4Final: VAN 2, EDM 4

Edmonton beat Vancouver 4-2, and Connor McDavid had three more assists, stretching his season-opening assist streak to 18 games, tied with Adam Oates for the second-longest in NHL history. Leon Draisaitl scored twice, on the power play and into the empty net, and now has 16 goals. Mattias Ekholm opened the scoring, Max Sasson tied it with nine seconds left in the first, and Jason Dickinson put Edmonton ahead 49 seconds into the third. Brock Boeser made it 3-2 with the goalie pulled at 17:25 before Draisaitl iced it. Devon Levi made 20 saves on 22 in his return; Leevi Meriläinen stopped 26 of 29. The Oilers are 12-3-3. The Canucks are 3-15-1 with seven points, and at this rate the only thing they'll lead the league in is mock drafts.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Saturday, November 7

Game recap

CBJ2BUF5Final: CBJ 2, BUF 5

Buffalo beat Columbus 5-2, and this one was settled by the middle of the second period. Josh Doan made it 5-1 at 10:53 of the second, and the rest of the night was a formality. Josh Norris scored twice, Jack Quinn opened it with his ninth, and Rasmus Dahlin added one. Owen Power had three assists and ran the game from the back end like he owned the building. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 24 of 26. Jet Greaves faced 37 shots and stopped 32, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke. Kent Johnson had a goal and an assist for the Blue Jackets, and Zach Werenski's power-play goal with 1:39 left was strictly for the fantasy crowd. The Sabres are 8-5-3. Columbus is 7-8-0, and its defense spent the second period watching Buffalo like it had paid for the tickets.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS1MIN4Final: SJS 1, MIN 4

Kirill Kaprizov had four points, and Minnesota beat San Jose 4-1 to stay first in the Central at 12-3-3. Kaprizov opened the scoring on a first-period power play for his 16th goal, then set up the next three: Maxim Shabanov on another power play in the second, Quinn Hughes in the third and Zach Bogosian, his first of the season. Hughes played 31 minutes and finished with three points, so apparently nobody in St. Paul has told him about shift lengths. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 of 24, and the only one he missed was Macklin Celebrini's goal that tied it 1-1 in the second. Yaroslav Askarov made 25 saves on 29 shots. The Sharks have lost four straight and are 7-10-1. Their coach told them this week to ignore the noise, which was easy enough: the loudest thing in the building was the Wild's power play.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5CGY3Final: ANA 5, CGY 3

Anaheim does its best work from behind, and Calgary was kind enough to set the table. The Flames led 3-1 after one period on goals from William Stromgren, Joel Hanley and a Joel Farabee power play, and Lukas Dostal was pulled after giving up three on 11 shots. Ville Husso came in and stopped all 10 he saw, and the Ducks went to work: Tristan Luneau in the second, Leo Carlsson on the power play 55 seconds into the third, then Cutter Gauthier with the winner, his 12th, with 1:34 left. Nikita Nesterenko's empty-netter made it 5-3. Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund had two assists each, and Dustin Wolf stopped 24 of 28. That's four straight wins for Anaheim, now 9-7-1. Calgary is 7-9-1 and just learned that a two-goal lead after 20 minutes is like a gift card: nice to have, gone by the weekend.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friday, November 6

Game recap

UTA4MTL5OTFinal: UTA 4, MTL 5 OT

Logan Cooley scored a hat trick and added an assist, Utah led three separate times, and the Mammoth still flew out of Montreal with one point. Cooley went 9, 10, 11 on the season, two of them on the power play, and Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal made it 4-3 early in the third. Every time, the Canadiens came back: Nick Suzuki (a goal, two assists), Arber Xhekaj, who scored his first and then dropped the gloves with Liam O'Brien four seconds later, Kirby Dach, and Adam Engstrom, whose first of the year tied it 4-4 with five minutes left. Cole Caufield needed 30 seconds of overtime for his 11th, set up by Lane Hutson and Suzuki. Jakub Dobes stopped only 16 of 20, Sebastian Cossa 30 of 35. Montreal is 10-3-3. Utah held the lead for most of the night and handed it back three times: that's not a lead, that's a timeshare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK2DET1Final: VGK 2, DET 1

Forty minutes of nothing, then a third period worth the price of admission, and Vegas took it 2-1 in Detroit. Anton Johansson finally broke the ice for the Red Wings two minutes into the third, and the lead lasted all of 2:18 before Braeden Bowman tied it. Then, with 1:42 left, Trevor Connelly buried his seventh from Jack Eichel and Rasmus Andersson, and the Little Caesars Arena crowd went home with cold pizza. Carter Hart was the reason it got that far, stopping 25 of 26, while Daniil Tarasov made 32 saves on 34 shots in a game the Wings had no business staying in. Vegas is 11-5-2. Detroit falls to 7-7-3, one goal on a night it needed two. Hockeytown has been rebuilding so long the blueprints are on microfiche.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI1TBL4Final: CHI 1, TBL 4

Tampa Bay is now 8-0 at home, and Chicago never looked like the team to change that. Victor Hedman opened it on the power play four minutes in, Ilya Mikheyev scored late in the first, and early in the third Ryan McDonagh and Mikheyev again made it 4-0 inside three minutes. Zemgus Girgensons came back from his lower-body injury ahead of schedule and set up Mikheyev's second. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26, and the one he missed was Roman Kantserov's with 50 seconds left, which is the closest thing to a highlight the Blackhawks had. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second. Arvid Soderblom made 31 saves on 35 shots. The Lightning are 10-3-2. Chicago is 4-12-1, and in a rebuild like this, spoiling the shutout counts as a win.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4NJD5OTFinal: STL 4, NJD 5 OT

New Jersey led 4-1 after two periods and still needed Jesper Bratt in overtime. The Devils built it with a goal from Luke Hughes, two from Anthony Mantha and one from Jesper Boqvist, with Mantha's second coming 19 seconds after Boqvist's; Jack Hughes had two assists. Then St. Louis woke up. Mason McTavish scored midway through the third, Philip Broberg made it 4-3, and Dalibor Dvorsky tied it 18 seconds later with 5:06 to go. Bratt settled it 1:26 into overtime, from Dougie Hamilton. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 28 of 32, and Jordan Binnington made 31 saves on 36 shots. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the second. The Devils are 11-5-0. The Blues scored three goals in 3:08 to rescue a game they'd spent two periods losing, then got a loser point for it, which is the most St. Louis outcome possible.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR5NYI3Final: CAR 5, NYI 3

Carolina scored twice in the first 3:20, the Islanders tied it twice, and the league's best team won it anyway, 5-3 at UBS Arena. Logan Stankoven scored 57 seconds in and Jesperi Kotkaniemi added another. Mitchell Chaffee (his first) and Brayden Schenn tied it early in the second; Andrei Svechnikov put Carolina back in front a minute later, and Victor Eklund tied it again before the second intermission. The winner came from the least likely name on the sheet: William Carrier, his first of the season with 5:08 left, from Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho. Jalen Chatfield added the empty-netter. Brandon Bussi stopped 24 of 27, Semyon Varlamov 34 of 38. The Hurricanes are 13-3-2. The Islanders, still without Mathew Barzal and Ryan Pulock, are 7-6-2, and they made their fans watch a fourth-liner decide it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI2NYR3Final: PHI 2, NYR 3

Philadelphia had a third-period lead at Madison Square Garden and gave it back in 89 seconds. Gabe Perreault scored first for the Rangers, then Simon Benoit (his first of the year) and Noel Acciari scored two minutes apart in the second to put the Flyers up 2-1. It held until 13:52 of the third, when Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play, and Tye Kartye won it at 15:21, with Adam Fox assisting on both. Dylan Garand stopped 23 of 25 for New York, and Joseph Woll made 25 saves on 28 shots for Philadelphia. The Rangers are 9-7-1. The Flyers fall to 4-10-4. For an offense that scores less than anyone, two goals is a hot streak, and they still couldn't hold it through the third.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS6PIT2Final: BOS 6, PIT 2

Justin Brazeau gave Pittsburgh a 1-0 lead nine minutes in, and Boston answered with six of the next seven goals. Pavel Zacha, Mark Kastelic and Elias Lindholm, unassisted, scored in the last eight minutes of the first. Nick Robertson got the Penguins back within 3-2 early in the second, then Zacha scored again, Morgan Geekie made it 5-2 and Fraser Minten added the sixth in the third. David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka each had two assists, both on Zacha's goals. Michael DiPietro only had to stop 16 of 18. At the other end, Arturs Silovs saw 24 shots and stopped 18, which is how you get to 5-9-2. The Bruins are 12-4-1. Pittsburgh's lead lasted three minutes and its defense never showed up, which is about how this season has gone for a franchise that keeps insisting it isn't rebuilding.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL1CBJ2SOFinal: DAL 1, CBJ 2 SO

Two goalies, 65 minutes and one goal each, and Columbus won the skills competition. Cam Talbot and Casey DeSmith made it scoreless through two periods, and Mikko Rantanen's ninth, from Wyatt Johnston, looked like enough for Dallas midway through the third. Then Zach Werenski scored his first goal of the season with 3:14 left, from Kent Johnson and Matthew Knies, and the Blue Jackets never trailed again. In the shootout Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored; Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin didn't. Talbot finished with 27 saves on 28 shots plus both shootout attempts, and DeSmith stopped 29 of 30. Columbus is 7-7-0 with two straight wins. Dallas, without Miro Heiskanen, is 9-5-2. The Stars put one puck past Talbot in 65 minutes and none in the shootout, and that offense couldn't pass a referendum either.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2WPG6Final: VAN 2, WPG 6

Winnipeg went nine games without a win; now it has two in a row, and Vancouver was happy to help. Alex Iafallo scored on the power play at 3:49 and Cole Koepke added another 14 seconds later. Liam Ohgren answered for the Canucks, but Dawson Mercer scored his first of the season before the first intermission, Neal Pionk and Mark Scheifele scored in the second, and Mario Ferraro made it 6-1 in the third. Kyle Connor and Dylan DeMelo each had two assists, and Scheifele had a goal and an assist. Brock Boeser scored late. Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 26 for the Jets, and Leevi Meriläinen gave up six on 29 shots. Winnipeg is 6-8-3. Vancouver is 3-14-1, the league's worst, and has become the team you play when you need to feel good about yourself again.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5EDM4Final: ANA 5, EDM 4

Pavel Mintyukov had the full Gordie Howe hat trick, and Anaheim held on in Edmonton, 5-4. Cutter Gauthier opened it on the power play, Evan Bouchard answered on one, and Connor McDavid scored shorthanded early in the second to make it 2-1 Oilers. Then the Ducks scored four straight: Mintyukov twice, his first two of the season, three minutes apart, and Beckett Sennecke twice, the second on the power play early in the third. Mintyukov also set up Sennecke's first and fought Kasperi Kapanen in the first period. Edmonton came back late: Kapanen on the power play, then Leon Draisaitl at 19:15 with the goalie pulled, but time ran out. McDavid had a goal and two assists. Laurent Brossoit stopped 23 of 27; Matt Tomkins 16 of 21. Edmonton is 11-3-3. Five goals on 21 shots: the Oilers' goaltending search goes on, now in its second decade.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3COL2OTFinal: NSH 3, COL 2 OT

Nashville goes past regulation again, and this time Steven Stamkos made it count. Ross Colton opened the scoring, Jaden Schwartz tied it, Vitali Pinchuk put the Predators back in front with his first of the season, and Parker Kelly tied it early in the second. After that, nothing for 37 minutes, until Stamkos scored on the power play 2:18 into overtime, from Roman Josi and Ryan O'Reilly. Justus Annunen was the story in the Nashville net, stopping 30 of 32 at Ball Arena, while Mackenzie Blackwood made 22 saves on 25 shots. Colorado tried a new top pair, with Sam Malinski beside Devon Toews and Cale Makar moved to Brett Kulak's side, and got two goals out of 32 shots for the trouble. The Predators are 7-4-5. The Avalanche, 9-6-2, have one of the league's best attacks and got outscored by Vitali Pinchuk and Ross Colton.
